He didn't teach a single class on success until he'd already done over $10 billion in sales.

Not a typo — ten billion, first, then the course. Compare that to the guy teaching "how to buy real estate with no money down" who'd personally only closed a couple of deals and made his real money selling the course instead. One of them actually did it. One of them just talked about it convincingly. The entire difference in who's worth listening to sits right there.

An archer named Arjuna rode his chariot into the middle of a battlefield to see exactly who he'd be fighting.

Cousins. Former teachers. Neighbors he'd grown up beside. His own family, on both sides, about to kill each other. He put down his bow and said the words nobody in that text had said before him: I am your disciple — instruct me. That single sentence is the oldest teaching there is on how anyone actually learns anything. You cannot be taught a thing you already think you understand.

A student once stormed into a teacher's room demanding to be taught the secret of enlightenment on the spot.

The teacher didn't answer. He picked up a teapot and kept pouring into the student's cup — past full, over the rim, onto the floor. "My cup is full, master," the student said. "Why do you keep pouring?" The teacher never stopped. Your mind is already that full, he said. Pour more truth into it and it just runs onto the floor.

A mind that already thinks it knows can't receive anything new.

Every magnet has two poles. Science says your own body is one too.

Stand upright and your head carries the north pole, your feet the south. Stand near someone with more energy than you, and the oldest teachers already knew where to put your head: down, at their feet — because that's the exact position that lets you draw their field into yours. It's not submission. It's wiring two magnets so the current can actually flow. That's the real reason monks and masters bow.

People ask how someone already enlightened could still bow down to another teacher. Here's the answer: the same way Jesus did.

He bowed down and let himself be baptized by John the Baptist — one teacher bowing to another. The greatest ones never stop humbling themselves and never stop filling back up. There's an old line for why: the wise man learns from the fool, but the fool never learns from the wise man. The moment you decide you already know, you stop being able to receive anything at all.
